highlights.title: Checks in more editors
highlights.body: Google Docs (with Tools › Accessibility › braille support on), Notion, LibreOffice Writer, Pages and VS Code are now checked as whole documents, with underlines on every line you see.

highlights.title: The card moves on to the next fix
highlights.body: After you apply a fix, the card glides to the next one instead of closing. Click a dot under the card to jump straight to that fix.

highlights.title: Popup opacity and underline wave
highlights.body: Settings › Appearance has two new sliders: how see-through the popups are, and how wavy the underlines look.

highlights.title: Report an issue in one click
highlights.body: Settings › About has a new look and a Report an issue button. It starts an email to support with your app and macOS versions already filled in.

items.text: Firefox: rich editors are read right after launch, and their paragraphs stay apart.
Obsidian: underlines follow the text as you scroll.
Your clipboard comes back after every applied fix, and when Meboki quits.
⌘Tab and other shortcuts work while fixes are being written.
Code blocks inside normal text are left untouched.
Safari: Apply all no longer stops halfway.
Slack and other apps that trim pasted text keep the space around an added word.
Popup shadows are no longer cut off at a rectangle.
Onboarding shows the whole Download button.

highlights.title: A switch for logs
highlights.body: Settings › Privacy › Logs turns logging on or off. Logs are now off by default, and so are text snippets in them.

items.text: Show Meboki Log opens the logs folder when there is no log yet.

highlights.title: Messages and Reminders are checked as you type
highlights.body: Underlines now show up in the Messages text box and in Reminders titles and notes, without pressing the shortcut.

items.text: LibreOffice: underlines and the card sit in the right place on a Mac with several displays.
Firefox and Thunderbird: fixes are pasted, so they always land on the right words.
